lines.arrive: A little town, on a still afternoon. You need to know the time.
lines.notice: Market day, Saturday. Choir practice, Thursday. A lost cat. Clock repairs, enquire within.
lines.bench: A bench in the sun. The whole town seems to be having a nap.
lines.reads: The town clock says two o'clock. It has always kept good time.
lines.asked: The postman looks at his watch. It's ticking.
lines.true: And the church bell strikes two. It is two o'clock.
lines.stopped: The town clock hasn't moved. It stopped at two o'clock yesterday. You happened to look at it in the one minute of the day it was right.
lines.end: You believed it. It was true. And you had good reason. So did you know what time it was?
lines.stopped_2: The town clock hasn't moved. It stopped yesterday, at two. If you'd looked at that, you'd have believed exactly the same thing.
lines.asked_end: But you asked someone whose watch was going. This time, you weren't only right.
